Top left: a light green cross; an orange crossing on a light green dashed line (the crossing computed on it), above a light green line, with a blue and a black rung between the two orange lines. Top right: large disk (orange rim traced from the facsimile, a pencil circle just inside it, dashed where the pencil is broken) crossed by nine orange pseudolines traced strand by strand, numbered at their ends 1 ... 9 and 1' ... 9' as on the page (the transcription lists only 1, 2, 3, 1', 2', 3', 5, 6', 8', 9; the page also has 4, 4', 5', 6, 7, 7', 8, 9'): strands 1, 2, 3 all leave one point of the rim at the top and all reach one point at the bottom, strands 6 and 7 share their two end points (left and right); these pairs do not meet inside, every other pair crosses exactly once inside the disk (32 crossings, checked on the drawn curves). Eleven yellow regions are bounded exactly by their strands and the rim. A short second orange stroke along the rim at the lower right; pencil arrow at the top; three small ink dots on the rim. Middle: disk with yellow-green rim crossed by ten black pseudolines traced strand by strand, ends numbered 0 ... 9 and 0' ... 9' as on the page: strands 0, 1, 2, 3 do not meet, every other pair crosses exactly once (39 crossings); around it the large pencil circle with three blue arcs (top, left, bottom: the page has no fourth), pencil fans at those arcs, a pencil arrowhead on the right and four pencil ticks across the circle. The five digit sequences are written out as on the page, the bracketed part underlined (the brackets are drawn as square brackets under the digits on the page); in the sequence below the orange disk a 7 and a 6 are written over each other near the end, with a pencil 6 on them (given as 7 6); the pencil scribbles under the top sequence are left out. Bottom left: an orange line, two light green lines and three orange lines (numbered 1 2 3 above and 3 2 1 below) all through one computed point, thin black lines and a black arrow, a red cross on the orange line, a pencil arrow; the pencil hatching along the lines is left out. Bottom middle: small disk, rim dark green on the left half and yellow-green on the right, blue-grey arcs between the ends of its three black strands at the top and at the bottom, ticks on the rim numbered 1, 0, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 2, 3, 9', 8', 7', 6', 5', 4' as on the page (the labels under the disk are cut by the crop; a small stroke like 1 inside the disk is left out). Bottom right, the braid, traced strand by strand from the facsimile: five nodes computed once (the node at the left, the two ends of the black segment on the green line, the two nodes at the right) and every red strand fitted to the ink between them: two arcs from the left node and one from the left end of the segment over to the upper right node, the lens above and below the black segment between its two ends, three strands from the blue stroke at the lower left (where the page has small dots and the digits 3, 2, 1) to the lower right node, one strand from the right end of the segment to each right node, a short strand from the left node ending on the blue stroke; the green arcs pass through the right nodes and the right end of the segment, the pale blue strokes through the two ends of the segment; inside the lens four short brown verticals and an orange cross; the lowest strand runs along the bottom edge of the crop. Still differs from the facsimile: the small digits written among the strands of the braid (round the right nodes and inside the lens) are not reproduced, and the joins of the strands just right of the left node, overinked by the blue stroke and the digits, are a reading. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Revised 2026-11-09 after Michel's check (#134): the drawing is right on the labels of the orange disk (also 4, 4', 5', 6, 7, 7', 8, 9'), on the three blue arcs of the pencil circle and on the order of the small disk's labels (1, 0, 4, 5, ..., 9). It stays partial only because the small digits among the strands of the braid are still not reproduced.
